Title: Power ON at Low speed
Objective: Confirm the fan starts and runs at lowest speed from OFF
Steps: 1) Plug into 220V; 2) Confirm OFF; 3) Press button 1; 4) Observe blades and airflow for 5s
Expected Result: Blades rotate smoothly within 2-3s at lowest airflow; button 1 stays latched; no rubbing noise
Actual Result: Blades started within ~2s at lowest airflow; button 1 stayed latched; smooth, no rubbing/grinding noise

Title: Power ON at Medium speed
Objective: Confirm Medium is a distinct higher level than Low
Steps: 1) From Low press button 2; 2) Compare airflow vs Low for 5s
Expected Result: Speed visibly/audibly increases above Low; button 2 latches and releases button 1; steady rotation
Actual Result: From Low pressed 2; airflow/speed increased above Low; button 2 latched and 1 popped out; steady, no abnormal noise

Title: Power ON at High speed
Objective: Confirm High delivers maximum airflow and runs stably
Steps: 1) From Medium press button 3; 2) Observe airflow, noise, vibration for 10s
Expected Result: Highest airflow of the three levels; stable rotation; vibration within limits; no abnormal noise
Actual Result: From Medium pressed 3; strongest of the 3 speeds; stable, minimal vibration, only normal noise

Title: Speed step-through Low-Med-High-Low
Objective: Verify the 3 speeds are distinct and selecting a new speed releases the previous
Steps: 1) Press 1 wait 5s; 2) Press 2 wait 5s; 3) Press 3 wait 5s; 4) Press 1 again wait 5s
Expected Result: Three clearly different airflow levels; each press latches exactly one button and pops the previous; no buzzing or stall
Actual Result: Stepped 1-2-3-1; three distinct levels; each press latched one button and released the previous; immediate transitions, no buzzing/stall; blades fine. Note: worn front grille free-spun from airflow (not via SWING) - separate finding, see TC-13/bug log

Title: Front-grille SWING rotation ON
Objective: Verify the front grille rotates (sweeps airflow direction) when SWING is pressed
Steps: 1) Run at Medium (button 2); 2) Press SWING; 3) Watch front grille for at least 3 full rotation cycles
Expected Result: Front grille rotates smoothly and continuously without binding or stalling; SWING stays latched; fan speed unaffected
Actual Result: SWING off: worn grille already drifted slowly clockwise from airflow (worn-grille defect). Pressing SWING reversed it to slow counter-clockwise, against the wind - confirms SWING actively drives rotation. But not smooth: worn grille sometimes let the wind win, slipping clockwise then back CCW. SWING stayed latched; speed unaffected

Title: Button 0 releases all latched buttons (master OFF)
Objective: Verify 0 simultaneously releases the active speed button and SWING; confirm 0 is the only master release and SWING has no independent off (usability limitation)
Precondition: Fan running at Low with SWING engaged (grille rotating)
Steps: 1) Press 1 (Low); 2) Press SWING (grille rotating); 3) Confirm both buttons latched down; 4) Press 0; 5) Observe all buttons, grille, blades
Expected Result: Pressing 0 pops out both the speed button and SWING at once; blades coast to a stop and grille rotation stops; no button stays latched (usability limitation: SWING has no independent off, and 0 also switches the fan off)
Actual Result: Pressed 1 (Low) then SWING - both latched. Pressing 0 released both buttons at once; blades coasted to a stop and grille rotation stopped; no button remained latched. Confirms 0 is the single master release

Title: Power OFF (button 0)
Objective: Verify the fan stops completely when OFF is pressed
Steps: 1) From any speed press button 0; 2) Observe until blades stop
Expected Result: All speed buttons release; motor de-energizes; blades coast to a full stop within a few seconds; silent after
Actual Result: From a running speed pressed 0; speed button released, motor de-energized, blades coasted to a full stop within a few seconds; silent afterward

Title: Head vertical tilt holds angle
Objective: Verify the head tilts up/down and holds the set angle
Steps: 1) Tilt head upward while running; 2) Release and observe 30s
Expected Result: Friction joint holds the chosen angle without drooping; airflow redirected; no cracking or slipping
Actual Result: Tilted head up ~20deg; friction joint held the angle without drooping; airflow redirected; no cracking or slipping

Title: Continuous-run endurance 30 min at High
Objective: Verify thermal and mechanical stability over a sustained run
Steps: 1) Set High; 2) Run 30 min; 3) Touch housing, listen for new noise, check speed steady
Expected Result: Runs full 30 min with no auto-shutoff or slowdown; housing warm but not scorching; no burning smell; no new rattle
Actual Result: Ran High 30 min continuously; no auto-shutoff or slowdown; housing warm but comfortable to touch; no burning smell; no new rattle; speed steady

Title: Stability and vibration on flat surface
Objective: Verify the fan does not walk or tip from vibration at High
Steps: 1) Place on smooth flat table; 2) Run High 2 min; 3) Mark base position and check movement
Expected Result: Base stays put (feet grip); minimal vibration; unit does not creep or tip over
Actual Result: Ran High 2 min on a flat surface; base stayed put (feet gripped); minimal vibration; no creeping or tipping

Title: Simultaneous multi-button press
Objective: Determine behavior when two speed buttons are pressed at the same instant
Steps: 1) From OFF press buttons 1 and 3 simultaneously; 2) Note which latches and resulting speed; 3) Listen for buzzing, check breaker
Expected Result: Mechanical interlock latches only one winding; fan runs at one defined speed; no buzzing, no dual-winding energization, no breaker trip
Actual Result: Pressed 1 (Low) and 3 (High) at the same instant: neither button latched and the fan did not start (stayed OFF). Releasing both did nothing. No buzzing, no dual-winding energization, no breaker trip. The mechanical interlock blocks both from seating at once, so a simultaneous press is safely rejected (fail-safe to OFF) rather than one speed winning - differs from the predicted single-latch but meets all safety criteria

Title: Open / remove the front grille and reassemble
Objective: Verify the front grille opens/removes for cleaning and reattaches securely, and SWING + airflow still work
Input: Rotate the front grille lock to release grille, lift off, refit and re-lock
Steps: 1) Press 0 and unplug; 2) Rotate the front grille lock to release the grille and lift it off; 3) Inspect blades and refit grille, turn lock back until it seats; 4) Plug in, run Low, press SWING
Expected Result: Grille releases by rotating the lock without excessive force and re-seats firmly when locked back (no gap, does not detach); fan runs normally; SWING still works
Actual Result: Opened grille by rotating the front grille lock - released and lifted off easily, re-attached and re-locked normally with no gap or rattle; fan ran normally at Low and SWING engaged. Only anomaly: pre-existing worn-grille free-spin/slip when SWING and blades both run (see TC-05/bug log) - unaffected by reassembly and out of scope here

Title: SWING rotation independence from fan speed
Objective: Verify SWING grille drive works independently of speed buttons (incl. at OFF), persists across speed changes, and is cleared only by button 0
Steps: 1) At OFF press SWING and note if grille rotates with no airflow; 2) Press 1 then 3 while SWING engaged; 3) Press 0 (only control that clears SWING)
Expected Result: Rotation continues uninterrupted across speed change 1->3; SWING stays latched when speed changes; pressing 0 is the only way to clear SWING and it stops the fan too (record whether grille rotates at speed 0)
Actual Result: Pressing 0 releases all latched buttons (per TC-06). SWING only at speed 0 (no airflow): grille rotated normally under SWING power alone - SWING drive is independent of the blade motor (answers the open question: yes it rotates at speed 0). SWING stayed latched across speed change and was cleared only by 0 - control independent of speed. Deviation at HIGH: strong airflow overpowered the worn SWING drive and forced the grille to rotate backwards (wind direction) - same worn-grille defect as TC-05, dominant at high speed

Title: Finger guard safety (grille gap)
Objective: Verify grille/cage spacing (front grille and rear cage) prevents a finger reaching the blades
Precondition: Fan OFF and unplugged; 12 mm rod/pencil/finger
Input: 12 mm rod or finger through front and back openings, blades OFF
Steps: 1) Press 0 and unplug (test with blades OFF for safety); 2) Measure widest opening in front grille and rear cage; 3) Try to pass 12mm rod/finger through widest front and back openings toward the blade path
Expected Result: All openings (front grille and rear cage) < 12 mm; with fan de-energized the probe/finger cannot reach the blade path from any opening (if a finger/pencil can reach a blade = Fail/safety defect)
Actual Result: Tested with fan OFF and unplugged (blades stationary). Defect is on the rear cage: several cracks/gaps large enough to fit a finger through, so a finger can reach the blade path from the back - a finger could contact the blades while running. Front grille was not the problem area

Title: Steep-tilt / tip-over behavior
Objective: Verify safe behavior when the running fan is tilted far past normal
Precondition: Fan running at Medium on flat surface
Steps: 1) Run at Medium; 2) Carefully tilt entire fan to ~45 deg, hold 5s; 3) Watch blade-cage contact, any tilt cutoff, base lift; 4) Return upright
Expected Result: No blade-to-cage contact at angle; cage does not deform; fan keeps running safely OR powers down if tilt-cutoff equipped (record which); no grinding
Actual Result: Tilted the running fan to ~45deg and held; no blade-to-cage contact and no grinding; cage did not deform. No tilt cut-off fitted - the fan kept running normally at the tilted angle. On returning upright it continued running normally
